training_data: ADNI (ADNIMERGE + RECMHIST), 494 cognitively normal participants with at least one follow-up (389 censored / 105 converted to MCI); stratified 90/10 train/test split with nested 10x5-fold CV
test_data: AIBL (Australian Imaging, Biomarker & Lifestyle study), 320 CN participants (290 censored / 30 converted), plus the 10% ADNI hold-out
reason: The Fast RSF trained on ADNI (FS1) was applied unchanged to AIBL, an Australian cohort from a different consortium that played no part in training (C-index 0.73). A second model, retrained on ADNI with only the 17 shared features, gave 0.75 on AIBL, and a sensitivity analysis with multiple imputation in AIBL gave 0.77. A fixed model on a cohort from another consortium and country is V4. Caveat: five of the model's top-10 features are not collected in AIBL and were zero-filled in stage 1.

quotes.quote: In the first stage, we applied the original top-performing model—trained on the full ADNI feature set (FS1)—to the AIBL dataset after aligning feature dimensions by adding missing variables with neutral values. This resulted in a C-index of 0.73, demonstrating robust predictive performance and highlighting the model’s consistent capabilities across datasets.
The fast random survival forest model was retrained using these shared features and achieved a C-index of 0.79 on the ADNI test set and 0.75 on the AIBL dataset.
The dataset is first divided into training and testing sets in a stratified manner, with a ratio of 90% for training and 10% for testing as shown in Fig. 4.
